observations: Original Xbox One console (black) with a split matte and glossy top surface.
One black Xbox One wireless controller.
The console features a front-loading disc slot on the left side.
A warning sticker is visible on the front left of the console.
No power adapter (power brick) or cables are visible in the photos.
No game discs or cases are visible.

claims.evidence: photo 0 and 1 show the hardware design of the original Xbox One.
No physical discs are shown, and no screen capture of a digital library is provided.
Requires testing with a known working power supply to determine if the fault is the brick or the console.

risks.risk: The 'adaptor issue' may actually be a failure of the console's internal power circuitry or motherboard.
risks.proof: A video showing the console booting to the home screen using a functional power supply.

risks.risk: The mentioned games may be digital licenses tied to the seller's account, which cannot be safely transferred.
The controller may have mechanical issues like stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used in a 'button test' or 'calibration' menu.

risks.risk: The internal hard drive capacity is unknown (500GB vs 1TB).
risks.proof: A photo of the 'Storage' section in the system settings.

risks.risk: The optical disc drive may be unable to read or eject discs.
risks.proof: A video of a disc being inserted, loaded, and the game starting.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive

proof_requests: Video of the console successfully booting to the dashboard with a working power adapter.
Photos of the physical game discs mentioned.
Photo of the system storage screen showing the hard drive capacity.
Video demonstrating the controller working without stick drift.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as an original Xbox One. Because the seller admits to a power issue and provides no proof of operation, it is priced at the worst-case scenario as a non-working unit for parts with no games.
